title: parse shifts explicit UTC timestamps during a local DST gap
body:
## The problem

We get a one-hour shift when `parse` reads an explicit UTC timestamp with `TZ=America/New_York`.

### 💻 Code demonstrating the problem

From a checkout of the version below:

```sh
TZ=America/New_York node --experimental-strip-types --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { parse } from './pkgs/core/src/parse/index.ts'
console.log(parse('2024-03-10T02:30:00Z', "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssX", new Date(0)).toISOString())
JS
```

### 🙁 Actual behavior

We get `2024-03-10T03:30:00.000Z` (`1710041400000` ms) from the [current parser](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/blob/717ce0a807ea4c6b540d015b5c408723175b2838/pkgs/core/src/parse/_lib/parsers/Hour0to23Parser.ts#L28-L35).

### 🙂 Expected behavior

`2024-03-10T02:30:00.000Z` (`1710037800000` ms), as [documented for `X`/`Z`](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/blob/717ce0a807ea4c6b540d015b5c408723175b2838/pkgs/core/src/parse/index.ts#L217-L226).
This UTC instant is the previous evening in New York, outside the gap.

## Debug information

Versions: core 4.4.0 at [717ce0a807ea4c6b540d015b5c408723175b2838](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/commit/717ce0a807ea4c6b540d015b5c408723175b2838), Node 22.20.0 and 24.8.0, esbuild 0.25.10, source and production ESM, TZ=America/New_York.

The hour setter appears to normalize `02:00` locally before the [offset setter](https://github.com/date-fns/date-fns/blob/717ce0a807ea4c6b540d015b5c408723175b2838/pkgs/core/src/parse/_lib/parsers/ISOTimezoneWithZParser.ts#L37-L46) runs.

Happy to send a fix.

— [ChipLab](https://chiplab.donmakino.com/findings#clab-2026-1230)
